```dockerfile
# Stage 1: Install dependencies
FROM node:22-alpine AS deps
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --ignore-scripts

# Stage 2: Build
FROM node:22-alpine AS builder
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=deps /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY . .
RUN npm run build

# Stage 3: Production
FROM node:22-alpine AS runner
ENV NODE_ENV=production
WORKDIR /app

COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --omit=dev --ignore-scripts && npm cache clean --force

COPY --from=builder /app/dist ./dist

RUN addgroup -S appgroup && adduser -S appuser -G appgroup
USER appuser

EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "dist/index.js"]
```

**Why each decision:**

- **`node:22-alpine`** — alpine base cuts image size from ~1GB (full Debian) to ~150MB.
- **Separate `deps` stage** — caches the `npm ci` layer so rebuilds skip dependency install when only source files change.
- **`npm ci` over `npm install`** — deterministic, faster, and respects `package-lock.json`.
- **`--omit=dev` in runner** — excludes devDependencies (TypeScript, ts-node, etc.) from the final image.
- **`npm cache clean --force`** — removes the npm cache that `npm ci` leaves behind in the layer.
- **Non-root user** — running as `appuser` limits blast radius if the container is compromised.
- **Only `dist/` copied into runner** — TypeScript source, `node_modules` from build stage, and all tooling stay out of the final image.

**Assumptions to adjust for your project:**

| Assumption | Where to change |
|---|---|
| Entry point is `dist/index.js` | `CMD` line |
| Build script is `npm run build` | Stage 2 `RUN` |
| App listens on port 3000 | `EXPOSE` line |
